name: Mention NO (retail overpays 'will he say X')
description: Sells YES (buys NO, taker) on 'What will Donald Trump say during <event>?' word markets when the YES bid is 10-90c, shortly after the market starts trading, and holds to settlement. Retail buys the YES lottery ticket on words that are said only ~36% of the time.
hypothesis: On the 150-market backfill sample (86 events, Jan-Aug 2026) the first YES price of a mention market is 14c too high at 10-90c (outcome rate 36% vs mean price ~50%; t=3.2 clustered by event, both halves negative), and a taker selling YES at the proven bid nets +6.5c after fees (t~1.7, 133 markets). Counterparty: retail buying the headline word. Wrong if the full-history walk-forward CI (net of fees) <= 0 or the lockbox loses.
